title: Columbia's artist bureau, Sonny Werblin and MCA vaudeville dates
summary: When Columbia gave up its bureau she dealt with Sonny Werblin and MCA, with disappointing theater dates in a few cities.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I don't know whether I mentioned this before or not, but during the time when I was making my earlier recordings, I was under exclusive contract to Columbia Records.
And there was a situation in which
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Columbia had to give up their artist bureau.
Oh yes, we discussed briefly.

Right. And because of monopolistic tendencies. When I was with Columbia, I had access to radio, recordings, and personal appearances -- that is, vaudeville. And this was just too much power for one company to have. So, Columbia had to give up their artist bureau. And most of the artists that were with Columbia were assigned to MCA. Well, at that time, Kirby was just beginning to work under the aegis of MCA. So I was called in by Sonny Werblin who was in the band department at that time -- See, MCA was noted for their exploitation of bands, and not necessarily art or vocals.
Sonny Werblin, just as a footnote, is known today as a sports impresario.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yes.
What is he, director of the Madison Square Garden --
I don't know, but he's pretty big these days. He has everything to do with Madison Square Garden.
And that's including New Jersey Meadowlands.
Yes.
The racetrack.
So anyway, I was called in -- and I think what they wanted to do was put together a Maxine Sullivan and John Kirby package so that we could make appearances together.

When we began to talk terms, I wasn't pleased with what Sonny Werblin was offering. And I think what he was trying to impress upon me was he fact that Kirby was just coming in. That is, he was going to be big, and that I was on my way out because I had been around for a few years. You know, I had been accepted nationally for a few years. So, I didn't like that attitude, so I just
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
said, you know, 'Well forget about the whole thing.' We did do appearances together. That is under separate arrangements.

But with MCA, we tried to do vaudeville appearances, but it was not a good package. For number one, the band was a small combination; and although I was a featured vocalist, the act was not strong enough to take over the stage in a production if there was not enough variety.

And they tried to sell Kirby and myself as the attraction in the theater. And we just weren't strong enough to carry a whole program, You know, in a vaudeville house, you got to have acrobats, comedians, and things like that. So it didn't work.
I think we did about maybe four theaters. We played out in Indianapolis, and around in some of the not-so-big houses. But it didn't jell.
(End of Tape 3A)
